implementationNotes:
Mechanism (mirrors src/lib/events/eventTypeLabels.ts, already GREEN and Bentham-reviewed in this repo): give each AUTH_PROVIDERS entry a `label` field that is a DIRECT reference to a compiled paraglide message function, e.g. `{ id: 'google', label: m.auth_provider_google }` (function value, not a call) — never a dynamic `m[`auth_provider_${id}`]` lookup, since paraglide message functions are statically analysed/tree-shaken and a template-literal key breaks that analysis (this is exactly why eventTypeLabels.ts uses an explicit object literal enumerating every key by name rather than building the map from a string list). `AuthProvider.label` becomes `() => string` instead of `string`; every render site changes `{provider.label}` to `{provider.label()}`. Import `{ m } from '$lib/paraglide/messages.js'` directly into providers.ts — already-proven to work in a plain .ts (non-.svelte) module via eventTypeLabels.ts and nav/entries.ts; no SSR concern since this app runs with `ssr = false` everywhere (Path C decision), so there is no server/client message-resolution split to worry about.

For the two providerLabel() call sites outside the three `.label`-consumer components (profile page's `identityProvider` at line 55 and the linked-identity row at line 901, whose input is an arbitrary live-Entu string, not guaranteed to be a current AUTH_PROVIDERS id), replace PROVIDER_LABELS/providerLabel with a resolver function built the same way as `eventTypeLabel()`: guard with `Object.hasOwn`-style lookup (a `Map`/`find` over AUTH_PROVIDERS by id works too) and fall back to the RAW id string for an unrecognized provider — never throw, never render blank, matching the existing PROVIDER_LABELS fallback behavior (`id.charAt(0).toUpperCase()+id.slice(1)`) or eventTypeLabels' plainer 'raw value wins' fallback; either is defensible but must be a conscious pick since a stale/legacy provider string (old localStorage lastProvider value, or an Entu entu_user.provider value from before a provider was ever added/renamed) is a real, reachable input, not a hypothetical.

Open, un-resolved design tension that a straight-line 'reuse the same label everywhere' implementation will silently trip over: AUTH_PROVIDERS' google entry is CTA-phrased ('Continue with Google') while every other entry is a bare product/brand noun (Smart-ID, Mobile-ID, ID-card, E-mail, Apple) — this asymmetry predates this task and is untouched by #206/#219. The linked-identity row (an informational 'this account is linked' list item, not a button) and the identityProvider banner ('Signed in as X via Y') are DISPLAY-NOUN contexts, not CTA contexts. Gama's own framing — 'exactly one place a provider's display name comes from' — reads as wanting ONE label per provider, which would mean either (a) normalizing google's canonical AUTH_PROVIDERS text to the bare noun 'Google' and letting the three CTA surfaces (login, invite, link-picker) add their own static 'Continue with '/equivalent framing text around `{provider.label()}` in the template (keeps one Paraglide key per provider, changes visible CTA copy on three surfaces), or (b) keeping a CTA-form key distinct from a display-form key per provider (satisfies 'do not add a second provider LIST' literally — AUTH_PROVIDERS stays the one array — but is two labels per entry, arguably violating the spirit of 'exactly one place a display name comes from'). Neither option is dictated by the issue text or Gama's comment; this needs a PO/Gama call before RED, not an implementer's unilateral pick — see openQuestions.

Locale files: add exactly the new keys chosen (minimum 6, one per provider id — `auth_provider_smart_id`, `auth_provider_mobile_id`, `auth_provider_id_card`, `auth_provider_e_mail`, `auth_provider_google`, `auth_provider_apple`, naming vocabulary-neutral per architecture-decisions.md's anti-vertical-lock-in rule) to all four of messages/en.json, et.json, lv.json, uk.json (currently 497 keys each, perfectly in sync — Done-when's 'non-empty in all four locale files' is directly checkable the same way #205's existing spec pattern does it, per the issue text). Per the issue's own note, Smart-ID/Mobile-ID/ID-kaart/ID-card stay untranslated product names in every locale (same literal string in all four files is expected and correct, not a translation gap) while Google/E-mail/Apple's surrounding copy gets translation judgment — 'Continue with Google' itself, if kept as the canonical string, would need translating too (i.e., is NOT a bare product name), which is a further argument for option (a) above since a bare 'Google' needs no translation loop at all.

Test-layer requirement, not just observation: architecture-decisions.md:718 ('Tallis RED triggers: any spec touching new user-facing copy must assert the string comes from a m.*() call, not a literal in the template') means a RED spec for providers.ts should follow eventTypeLabels.spec.ts's exact pattern — hand-mock $lib/paraglide/messages.js with per-key DISTINCT marker strings (`auth_provider_google: () => '[msg:google]'`) and assert AUTH_PROVIDERS[i].label() === that marker, proving the value is NOT a hardcoded literal surviving in providers.ts. happy-dom can further assert, at the four consumer sites, that DOM textContent contains the resolved marker/label after rendering (matching the existing convention in page.signin-picker.spec.ts / page.profile-linked-accounts.spec.ts of querying by data-testid and reading textContent) — happy-dom has no layout engine but text-content assertions are exactly what it CAN reliably do (per the responsive-contract caveat elsewhere in architecture-decisions.md, which only disqualifies happy-dom for computed-layout/visibility claims, not text content).

implementationNotes: AUTH_PROVIDERS should NOT carry a bare dynamic-string key that gets indexed as `m[key]()` at each of the 3-4 render sites — that scatters dynamic property access across files and loses literal-call-site traceability. Recommended shape: keep `AuthProvider { id, labelKey }` in providers.ts (labelKey typed as a literal union or `keyof typeof m` for svelte-check to catch typos), but export ONE resolver function alongside AUTH_PROVIDERS — e.g. `resolveProviderLabel(id: string): string` — implemented as a switch/lookup of LITERAL `m.auth_provider_google()`-style calls (one per provider id), not a dynamic `m[...]` indexing. All five consumers (login CTA, invite CTA, profile link-picker CTA, profile linked-identity row, profile signed-in-as line via providerLabel) import and call this single function — this is what actually satisfies Gama's "exactly one place a provider's display name comes from," since it collapses both the AUTH_PROVIDERS-driven sites AND the old PROVIDER_LABELS-driven sites into one function. Estonian eID product names (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID/ID-card) still get keys per the issue's own note (for consistency/extraction) even though their translated value should stay the product name in every locale. For RED, mirror the two existing four-locale key-presence exemplars (page.profile-whole-field.spec.ts:519-531 `describe`+for-loop form, or page.profile-linked-accounts.spec.ts:907-937 `it.each` form) for the new keys, and mirror page.session-expired.spec.ts:98-108's `overwriteGetLocale(() => 'et')` + exact-match-against-`etMessages.<key>` pattern for asserting the new login-page copy actually renders the locale file's string (happy-dom can assert exact textContent/attribute values and DOM structure; it has no special i18n hooks beyond that — locale switching is entirely via `overwriteGetLocale`).
